items.title: Give the public front door and legal shell a real Sewer Night / Porcelain Day theme system.
items.why: Live source inspection found no theme state, toggle, token layer, or query/storage contract. HomeV2 is hard-coded to a dark radial surface and public/legal.css declares dark-only color-scheme, so CANON-047 is unmet and a screenshot harness alone would only automate the gap.
items.recipe: Create a pure shared theme contract with two project-specific palettes, URL override, durable preference, system fallback, DOM application, and accessible toggle. Tokenize the primary HomeV2 shell/cards/actions plus all legal pages, preserve the dark combat canvas for readability, and test resolution/persistence semantics and public-page parity.

L1.recipe: Add a toggle and swap the page background.

L2.recipe: Add durable theme tokens across HomeV2 and legal pages with focused tests.

L3.recipe: Ship two branded palettes, URL/storage/system resolution, accessible semantics, cross-surface parity, reduced-motion handling, and visual verification hooks.

items.title: Make theme and mobile-parity claims reproducible against an isolated staging URL.
items.why: The app has a pinned and installed @playwright/test dependency plus a one-off launch screenshot script, but no release receipt covering both themes, 390/768/1440 widths, legal surfaces, overflow, console failures, action visibility, or contrast. The app-release gate therefore has no durable CANON-041/047 evidence.
items.recipe: Build a repo-local Playwright audit command that targets an explicit URL, captures the front door and legal pages across three widths and both themes, checks horizontal overflow, visible primary action/theme control, page/console errors, and computed foreground/background contrast, then writes screenshots and a machine-readable JSON receipt under output/playwright. Add pure evaluator tests and execute it against the Session 123 preview.

L2.recipe: Add route, overflow, action, and console assertions with a JSON receipt.

L3.recipe: Cover both themes, three widths, public/legal pages, contrast evaluation, deterministic artifact naming, and strict staged-release exit status.

items.title: Make every closeout command named by the local protocol executable inside this repo.
items.why: The recovered closeout had to bypass the repo because render-state-vector.mjs, compute-entropy.mjs, append-genome-snapshot.mjs, sanitize-claude-settings.mjs, and ops.mjs rescore are absent. protocol-drift-check does not probe them, so its green result is a false-negative against the actual closeout contract.
items.recipe: Add thin project-local proxies that locate the authoritative Studio Ops scripts and bind --project/--path to this repo without copying private policy. Add ops rescore routing, strengthen protocol-drift-check to require the closeout surface, test command construction and missing-control-plane failures, and correct the existing router typo.

L2.recipe: Centralize safe proxy resolution and route ops rescore.

L3.recipe: Add source/behavior tests, protocol drift enforcement, Windows-hidden execution, argument binding, and actionable failure messages.

items.title: Turn named competitive RNG streams into an inspectable post-run fairness fingerprint.
items.why: runRng.js can snapshot every named stream and build deterministic receipts, but App and DeathScreen never consume those exports. Players see same-seed competitive copy without a way to inspect which seed/streams were actually used, leaving the strongest trust mechanism stranded in tests.
items.recipe: Build a compact receipt from the live run snapshot at death, pass it through deathFlow, and show seed, stream draw counts, and a stable fingerprint inside the existing secondary analysis disclosure. Label it as deterministic decision-stream evidence—not full physics replay proof. Add pure snapshot/prop/presenter tests and preserve RUN THE FIX as the first action.

L1.recipe: Show the run seed and total RNG draws.

L2.recipe: Add named-stream counts and a stable compact fingerprint.

L3.recipe: Wire the live snapshot end to end, add honest proof-language boundaries, accessible details, telemetry-ready shape, and regression tests.

items.title: Prove mission streak continuity across leap years, month/year rolls, and local daylight-saving boundaries.
items.why: The recovered dashed-key defect showed that four example dates were not enough to protect a calendar-based retention loop. The pure local-date contract can be saturated cheaply across thousands of consecutive dates without adding runtime cost.
items.recipe: Add a twelve-year consecutive-local-day invariant test that crosses leap days, month/year boundaries, and daylight-saving transitions at local noon while preserving the YYYY-MM-DD key shape and monotonically advancing the streak.

L1.recipe: Add explicit leap-day and New Year examples.

L2.recipe: Sweep a twelve-year local calendar window with a pure invariant.

L3.recipe: Run the same sweep under multiple process time zones in CI.

items.title: Make isolated session previews a first-class GitHub Actions path instead of depending on a developer's global Wrangler token.
items.why: Both locally available Cloudflare tokens failed the Pages API despite one being valid for DNS, while the production workflow already owns a correctly scoped Pages secret. The workflow only listens to main and hard-codes --branch=main, forcing production-before-staging or dashboard credential drift.
items.recipe: Allow bounded session-* pushes, derive the Pages branch and environment URL from github.ref_name, keep main behavior unchanged, and add a source-contract test. Use a temporary session branch for evidence, then push the same verified commit directly to main.

L2.recipe: Parameterize the Pages branch for session previews.

L3.recipe: Add bounded trigger patterns, dynamic environment evidence, regression tests, and preserve production semantics.
